clue.text: Line given by an old Roman

definitions.meaning: a reference line or level in surveying, from which heights are measured
the Latin word for 'given', as a Roman would have said it

explanation.surface: A Roman of antiquity supplies a line of verse or a boundary.
explanation.walkthrough: In surveying a datum is the fixed base line or level; in Latin the same word is the past participle 'given'.
explanation.definitionFit: Surveyors call their fixed base level a datum line, and Latin uses the word for something granted.

parts.note: postponing, and also read as a wedding band being put off until later

explanation.surface: Someone postpones the wedding plans.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as DEFER + RING, the word suggests postponing the engagement band.
explanation.definitionFit: Postponing something is delaying it to a later date.

indicators.note: a lisp turns the sound of S into TH, so the word is said with that change

parts.note: a ballad is a song

explanation.surface: A singer with a lisp finds the ballad a real chore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bind' looks like a nuisance; it is a binding, a strap such as a sandal thong.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow leather strap is used to tie or fasten things.

parts.note: describing something of the liquid element that shares its name with the innermost planet

explanation.surface: Something is said to belong to a metal from the planets.
explanation.walkthrough: Mercury is both the planet nearest the Sun and the liquid metal (quicksilver); the adjective describes compounds of that metal.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective names compounds of quicksilver, the metal that shares its name with a planet.

parts.note: a band that is not knotted like a tie, worn as dress by 'the cloth', the clergy

explanation.surface: A loose strip of fabric used as a bandage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The cloth' is a traditional name for the clergy; their white neckband fastens behind with a stud rather than being tied, so it is 'untied'.
explanation.definitionFit: A priest's stiff white neckband is part of clerical dress and is studded on, not knotted.

clue.text: Demand for performance for little money

definitions.meaning: a command to go ahead and act
an old small Dutch coin, so a trifling sum

explanation.surface: A performer asks for a fee and gets a pittance.
explanation.definitionFit: The two-word command 'go ahead' is also the old Dutch coin of tiny value.

clue.text: Lass has merit according to the writer

parts.note: gal is a girl or lass
S stands for 'has' shortened to 's
worthy means having merit

explanation.surface: A girl is deserving, says the author.
explanation.walkthrough: John Galsworthy (1867-1933) wrote The Forsyte Saga; 'according to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: John Galsworthy was a Nobel-winning English novelist and playwright.

parts.note: bits are the metal mouthpieces of a horse's bridle

explanation.surface: Some items carry either eyes or mouthparts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mouth-pieces' suggests speakers; it is a horse's bit.
explanation.definitionFit: The bony eye sockets of the skull hold the eyeballs.

parts.note: loath means reluctant or unwilling

explanation.surface: A speaker reluctantly finds something disgusting.
explanation.definitionFit: Something repellent and hateful is objectionable, exciting disgust.

definitions.meaning: cheats or swindles someone
black crows that nest in colonies

explanation.surface: Wool coats are taken from dark birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fleeces' looks like sheep's wool; it is the verb to swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: To swindle a victim is to cheat him, and the same word names the black crows.

clue.text: What a corny sort of meal we get here !

definitions.text: What a corny sort of meal we get here !

parts.words: What a corny sort of meal we get here
parts.note: a meal made from corn is ground grain, and the place that grinds it is the 'here'

explanation.surface: A diner grumbles about a trite, tasteless dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corny' suggests stale humour and 'meal' a dinner; here meal is ground grain made from corn.
explanation.definitionFit: Grain is ground into fine powder for baking at a mill, so the corny meal is produced there.

definitions.meaning: a cry of 'well done!' from an audience
a hired killer or desperado, an old Italian sense of the word

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a hitman deserves a round of clapping.
explanation.definitionFit: The shout of approval and the Italian word for a hired thug share a spelling.

clue.text: Stew's right — has a French taste

parts.note: goût is the French word for taste

explanation.surface: Someone named Stew is correct in having refined Continental preferences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stew' reads as a man's name; it is the definition, and its 's means 'is'. 'Has' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A highly seasoned meat and vegetable dish cooked slowly is a classic French stew.

indicators.note: the wise women come after the direction, so their letters are placed second

parts.note: S for south, a compass direction
witches were once called wise women

explanation.surface: Clever women follow along when the course alters.
explanation.definitionFit: To swap or shift from one thing to another is to make a change, a verb in the third person.

clue.text: Collects a horse — note stage makeup

parts.note: gee-gee, GG, is a child's word for a horse
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: the word stage is given a new make-up, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone gathers a horse and notes the theatrical cosmetics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stage makeup' looks like greasepaint; 'makeup' rearranges the letters of 'stage' into GATES.
explanation.definitionFit: To gather things into a total or mass is to amass them.

parts.note: IN means in fashion
swingers are players of swing, a jazz style

explanation.surface: Trendy jazz musicians performed into extra hours.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket bowlers deliver balls in 'overs', so 'overtime' is the time of the overs; inswingers are deliveries that curve in towards the batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket balls that curve into the batsman are bowled during overs, each a set of six deliveries.

parts.note: a firearm set off by a tripwire, lying in wait for intruders without anyone pulling the trigger

explanation.surface: A self-firing arm for a surprise attack.
explanation.walkthrough: These firearms were rigged against poachers and fired when a trespasser touched the wire.
explanation.definitionFit: A trap firearm fires itself when a wire is tripped, ambushing an intruder.

definitions.meaning: a thin twisted line or string
a unit of volume for stacked firewood, 128 cubic feet

explanation.surface: Fetch a line so the timber can be gauged.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin twisted string is also the name of the stack unit used to sell firewood.

indicators.note: the letters are turned about, rearranged

explanation.surface: Police detectives are unhappier about being sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: CID is the British police Criminal Investigation Department; 'about' rearranges CID and SADDER.
explanation.definitionFit: Something thrown out or rejected has been dismissed.

parts.note: Stevenson's novel of a boy abducted, with its title put in American slang

explanation.surface: An American edition of a Stevenson tale.
explanation.walkthrough: RLS is Robert Louis Stevenson, author of 'Kidnapped'; American slang for kidnapped is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: American slang for abducted is a synonym of the title of Stevenson's novel 'Kidnapped'.

definitions.meaning: spilt blood, as from a wound
Kensington ... is a street in the Royal Borough of Kensington and Chelsea, in London

explanation.surface: Violence breaks out in a royal town.
explanation.walkthrough: Kensington and Chelsea is a London borough with the title 'Royal'; Kensington Gore, by the Albert Hall, lies in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Spilt blood is also the name of a London street in the royal borough, Kensington Gore.

clue.text: Pigeons made the best divine messengers

definitions.meaning: a breed of fancy pigeon with metallic plumage
angels of the highest rank, who carry God's messages

explanation.surface: Homing birds turn out to be superb heavenly couriers.
explanation.walkthrough: Pigeons carry messages, which makes the surface look like one sentence; the archangel is also a breed of fancy pigeon.
explanation.definitionFit: Chief angels such as Gabriel are top heavenly messengers, and the name is shared by a pigeon breed.

clue.text: It's time to pay up, master

definitions.meaning: read as two words, the subscription fee is owed
overcome or bring under control

explanation.surface: A subscriber is reminded that dues are owed to the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: SUB is short for subscription, the membership fee; split in two, the word says the sub is due.
explanation.definitionFit: To overpower or conquer is to master, a verb.

clue.text: I swear this tongue is bad

definitions.text: I swear this tongue is bad

parts.words: I swear this tongue is bad
parts.note: someone who swears uses foul words, so the speech is 'bad'

explanation.surface: A speaker vows that a particular tongue is poor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I swear' looks like an oath of truth, but it is the cursing that makes the speech bad; bad words are what swearing is.
explanation.definitionFit: A tongue is a system of speech, and swearing is called bad speech.

indicators.note: what the words contain, their content, gives the run of letters

explanation.surface: A song with unusually lavish lyrics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Content' means what is held within, not the material of the song; the run spans 'unusually rich'.
explanation.definitionFit: A short poem meant to be sung, or the words to a tune.

clue.text: Exalted story a part of Greece tells

parts.note: the attic is the top storey of a house, raised high

explanation.surface: A lofty tale, a piece of Hellas recounts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Story' means a storey of a building here, not a tale; the highest storey is the one under the roof.
explanation.definitionFit: The region round Athens is a historic district of Greece.

definitions.meaning: Socrates feigned ignorance to expose others' errors, a ploy named after him
read as 'like iron', made from the metal with a -y suffix

explanation.surface: The philosopher's technique turns out to be cold and hard.
explanation.walkthrough: Socratic irony is the pose of ignorance Socrates used in argument.
explanation.definitionFit: Feigned ignorance in debate is named after Socrates, and the word also reads as 'like iron'.

definitions.meaning: a ragged ridge left on metal after cutting
the rolled R of the Northumbrian or Scottish accent

explanation.surface: A northerner's speech has a harsh ring.
explanation.walkthrough: The Northumbrian burr is the throaty R of north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: A ragged metal ridge shares its name with a rolled R in regional speech.

indicators.note: the I'd comes after the dress-style, so its letters are placed second

parts.note: a rig is an outfit or style of dress

explanation.surface: Someone vows to obey a severe dress code.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflexible and exacting rules are stiff, unbending ones.

definitions.meaning: knocking on timber is the superstition people use to ward off bad luck
dry rotten timber used as tinder to start a fire

explanation.surface: Someone tries to get protection from an arsonist.
explanation.walkthrough: A fire-raiser looks like an arsonist; it is tinder, the dry punk wood that catches a spark.
explanation.definitionFit: Knocking on timber is the charm for warding off ill luck, and dry tinder kindles a blaze.

parts.note: a king Edward known for piety, and someone who admits guilt, owns up to sins

explanation.surface: King Edward owned up to something.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward the Confessor was the English king (died 1066) who founded Westminster Abbey; the title describes someone who admits his sins.
explanation.definitionFit: One who admits faults is named in the title of the saintly English king Edward.

parts.note: dry means dull and uninteresting
an ad is an advertisement

explanation.surface: A poet's songbird gets boring promotion.
explanation.walkthrough: In Keats's 'Ode to a Nightingale' the bird is the 'light-winged Dryad of the trees'.
explanation.definitionFit: Keats calls his nightingale a tree nymph in the opening stanza of his ode.
